title: Using cryoEM and cryoET to visualize membrane penetration of a non-enveloped virus
protocol: Maintain T175 flasks of BHK-21 cells until they reach 90% confluence.
Change the medium in each flask with 35 mL fresh DMEM containing FBS and antibiotics.
Add 5 mL of BTV stocks into each flask.
Gently shake the flasks to mix the virus.
Aliquot the medium containing the virus and store at -80°C.
Measure the titer of virus stock by plaque assay.
Use a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of about 0.03 each time.
Incubate flasks for approximately 70 hours in an incubator.
Observe infected cells frequently, noting changes to round shape compared to polygonal uninfected cells.
Harvest cells when the ratio of infected cells reaches around 80%.
Discard media and add 1.5 mL pre-chilled lysis buffer into each flask.
Collect cells using a cell scraper and combine them in a 50 mL tube.
Add lysis buffer to reach a total volume of 20 mL in the tube.
Pipette up and down several times to separate the cells.
Keep the sample on ice for 15 minutes.
Centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 10 minutes to pellet cell nuclei.
Load supernatant onto a double cushion with 4 mL of 66% (w/w) sucrose buffer and 10 mL of 50% (w/v) sucrose buffer.
Centrifuge the sample at 100,000 × g using an SW28 rotor for 1 hour at 4°C.
Remove the sample above the virus band.
Collect the virus band at the interface of the two sucrose cushions.
Dilute the collected band 10 times to a total volume of 10 mL in 20 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.8).
Use a flashlight to direct the position detection of the band.
Carefully remove the sample above the band.
Collect the band with a 1 mL pipet.
Pipette several times to separate the virus aggregation after adding N-Lauroylsarcosine sodium salt to a final concentration of 0.1%.
Incubate on ice for 10 min.
Centrifuge the sample at 16,000 × g for 10 minutes.
Add 1 mL of 30% (w/v) sucrose to the bottom of a new SW41 tube.
Slowly layer the supernatant from step 1 on top of the 30% sucrose.
Pellet the sample at 80,000 × g for 1 hour at 4°C in an SW41 Ti rotor.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 20 μL of 20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.8.
Prepare lipids for cryoEM using DOPC, DOPE, cholesterol, and LBPA in a molar ratio of 50:20:15:15.
Dissolve all lipids in chloroform at a concentration of 25 mg/mL.
Mix DOPC, DOPE, cholesterol, and LBPA in a glass vial using glass syringes.
Evaporate the chloroform under a nitrogen gas flow in a laboratory fume hood.
Remove remaining traces of solvent by placing the glass vial in a vacuum desiccator for 3 hours.
Hydrate the dried lipids in 250 μL liposome buffer.
Pipette the sample several times and transfer it to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Freeze-thaw the mixture five times in liquid nitrogen.
Extrude the mixture twenty-one times through a 0.2 μm polycarbonate membrane filter using a Mini Extruder.
Store liposomes at 4°C and use within one week.
Glow discharge thin continuous carbon film coated lacey grids in an easiGlow machine for 1 minute.
Add sodium citrate buffer (pH 5.5) to final concentration of 100 mM to titrate liposomes.
Apply 2 μL of purified BTV virion to a glow discharged grid and incubate for 1 minute.
Blot the grid manually with filter paper to remove most of the virus.
Add 2.5 μL of acidified liposomes to the grid.
Mount the grid into the Vitrobot.
Incubate the grid for another 30 seconds after adding liposomes.
Blot the grid for 20 seconds at 8°C with 15 blot force and 100% humidity.
Plunge-freeze the grid in liquid ethane using a Vitrobot Mark IV.
Turn on the Vitrobot and set the temperature to 8°C and humidity to 100%.
Wait for blot paper saturation for 20 minutes prior to use.
Apply virus to the grid before adding liposomes.
For grids of cryoET at low pH (pH 5.5), mix the liposomes with 10 nm gold beads before applying them to the grid.
Check the quality of the grid by a TF20 microscope.
If ice on the grid is too thick, increase blot time and blot force.
If virus concentration is low, purify the sample again (repeat steps 1–13).
If no interactions between the virus and liposomes are observed, incubate the virus and liposome for a longer time in step 24.
Freeze the rest of the virus sample with the same condition.
Store the grids in liquid nitrogen for long-term storage before data collection.
Load optimized grids to a Titan Krios electron microscope equipped with a Gatan imaging filter (GIF) Quantum LS and a Gatan K2 Summit direct electron detector.
Operate the microscope at 300 kV in super-resolution mode.
Align the microscope carefully.
Set up the data collection condition in SerialEM.
Create a full map of the grid at 135× magnification in search mode.
Select squares with proper ice thickness.
Take a medium magnification map at 4800× for each selected square.
In the medium magnification map, identify virus particles.
Record movies at high magnification on the selected targets which contain virus particles.
Set defocus to -1.8 to -2.6 μm for single-particle reconstruction.
Capture movies at a nominal magnification of 105,000× with a calibrated pixel size of 0.68 Å on the specimen level in super-resolution mode.
Fractionate total exposure time into 40 frames to achieve a dosage of 40–50 electrons/Å² on the specimen.
Determine the defocus values of micrographs by CTFFIND4.
Pick virus particles by ETHAN software and manually check for particles near image edges.
Extract a total number of 27,138 virus particles with a box size of 768× 768 pixels.
Bin extracted particles to 384× 384 pixels (2.72 Å/pixel) to speed up data processing in Relion 3.1.
Reconstruct the overall structure of BTV using icosahedral symmetry.
Subject the particles from step 36 into 2D classifications in Relion.
Select classes with high resolution features where some α helices are visible in 2D average.
Subject selected particles to 3D classification (K=4) by using icosahedral symmetry.
Select 15,224 good particles and subject them to a 3D auto-refinement with icosahedral symmetry.
Re-extract the particles with a box size of 768×768 pixels (1.36 Å/pixel) by using accurate center and orientation parameters.
Use viral particle images and corresponding icosahedral-related data STAR files in the next step.
Perform an icosahedral-reconstruction-guided sub-particle reconstruction workflow to obtain near-atomic resolution structures of VP5 at low pH (pH 5.5).
Generate an initial model from the extracted particles using relion_reconstruct command.
Subject the extracted particles to local refinement in Relion with a map from step 38d as the initial model.
Perform focused 3D classification without orientation search in Relion.
Generate a cylinder mask centered on VP5trimer 1.
Run 3D classification with skip align option in Relion, asking for 5 classes.
CTF refine particles (per-particle defocus, per-micrograph astigmatism, beamtilt and high order aberrations).
Perform 3D auto refinement of the particles.
Generate a soft mask that includes only the VP5 part.
Subtract the density outside of the soft mask from low-pH state raw sub-particles 2D images using Relion particle subtraction.
Run several rounds of focused 3D classification without orientation search with the mask to sort out particles with good stalk density.
Select 75,625 particles that meet the criteria in this step.
Select the corresponding original sub-particles without subtraction in Relion.
Subject the selected sub-particles to 3D auto-refinement to yield a final reconstruction at 4.0 Å.
Use the final reconstruction for model building of VP5 stalk in low-pH state.
Fit the anchoring domain structure of VP5 at pH 8.8 into the low-pH state map (3.4 Å).
Manually adjust the model in Coot according to the density map.
Build the stalk of VP5 according to the low pH focus map (4 Å) with guidance from the structure of pH 8.8.
Refine the model in real space according to the low-pH state map (3.4 Å) by Phenix.
Validate the model by wwPDB validation server.
Dock the refined atomic model of low-pH state into the cryoEM map for VP5 in IMS2.
Build the helices of unfurling domain in VP5 in Coot with guidance from the structure of pH 8.8.
Align the frames in each movie by MotionCor2.
Generate a stack file including all the images from the same tilt series using newstack program in IMOD.
Estimate defocus values of aligned images in each tilt series by CTFFIND4.
Reconstruct tilt series with IMOD 4.9 software package using selected gold beads.
Use estimated defocus value of each image as input for ctfphaseflip.
Generate two tomograms: one by weighted back projection and another by SIRT method.
Bin high-contrast SIRT tomograms 4× (10.2 Å/pixel) using binvol program of IMOD.
Select 33 tomograms with good alignment and contrast under low pH condition for further processing.
Further bin selected tomograms by 2× (5.1 Å/pixel) and 4× (10.2 Å/pixel).
Manually pick particles of VP5 stalks in IMOD.
Represent each particle by 2 points in a contour: one for the capsid-proximal end and another for the capsid-distal end of the stalk protruding from the virus capsid.
Pick totals of 107 and 100 particles for the membrane-free stalk and membrane-wrapped stalk, respectively.
Perform sub-volume averaging in PEET software using 4× binned tomograms initially.
Generate initial orientations from manually picked particles by using stalkInit.
Perform angular search with a cylindrical mask in PEET.
Symmetrize the particles to C3 along the particle Y axis by using ModifyMotiveList program in IMOD.
Align the symmetrized particles with finer range settings until convergence.
Upgrade refinement to 2× binned tomograms with model files resampled from 4× binning to 2× binning.
Run alignment again until convergence.
Calculate the resolutions of subtomogram averages by calcFSC in PEET.
